title: Undoing permute and expand
hints: permute's output axis k is the input's axis `p_k`. To undo it, input axis `p_k` must come back from output axis k.
So `inv.(p_k) <- k`. Check: for `[2; 0; 1]` that's `[1; 2; 0]`, and permuting by one then the other is the identity.
An axis was grown when it was 1 in `x_shape` and isn't 1 in `out_shape`. A size-1 axis that stays 1 wasn't grown, so nothing sums over it.

answer.explain: permute only moves numbers, so its gradient moves them back: `permute g` by the inverse order. The starter returns the order itself, which is right only when the permutation is its own inverse, like a transpose. expand copies a value along its grown axes, and every copy receives a share of the gradient, so the gradient sums over those axes. An axis that was already 1 and stays 1 is not a copy, which is the starter's other mistake.
